newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti completes PC transfer to Piedmont.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti completes PC transfer to Piedmont.

text.p: Italian hi-tech company Olivetti said the shares of O.P. Computers SpA, the company incorporated by Olivetti that bought Olivetti's Personal Computer business, were on Friday transferred to Piedmont International.

An Olivetti statement said the transfer follows the sale on March 31 of trade receivables and shares of foreign units to O.C.W. International, a wholly-owned unit of Piedmont, fully executing contracts signed in the PC business sale.
It said the aggregate price of the operation was equal to the net equity transferred, estimated at some 70 billion lire.
Olivetti will be entitled to a further payment based on a percentage of the company's profits over the next three years.

In order to simplify the previous relationship between the company being transferred and Olivetti, the parties agreed to offset reciprocal debt and credit. To settle any remaining financial credit, the Olivetti Group has withheld a corresponding amount of commercial receivables towards third parties in its own equity.
Olivetti reiterated that it will take a minor stake in the capital of Piedmont with an investment of $10 million.
The statement said the aggregate financial effect for the Olivetti Group of the sale of its PC business to Piedmont was around 250 billion lire.
